name: Professor Chill
description: This is a 30 minute live improvised performance using modular and other electronic instruments, looping technology, and with no computer or backing tracks involved. The performance is a mix of electronica, ambient and chill out influences, drawing on concepts from his 2025 Brain States album, exploring the Alpha State brain frequencies often associated with relaxation, trance, meditation, and mystical experience. Original ambient video material based on animated digital mandalas will be projected behind the performance creating an integrated audio-visual experience. The music will be diffused on 3D immersive sound through the HISS Sound System.
bio: Professor Chill is a longstanding fixture of the chillout scene, working since 1988 as both an electronic music producer and a qualified sound scientist. Unlike the colourific professors Green and Plum, he was awarded his very real title as a result of his academic career, having studied with composers such as Gavin Bryars and Katharine Norman, gaining the first ever PhD for composing popular music. He is Professor of Music and Head of Department of Humanities at the University of Huddersfield. His album Dub Archaeology was released in 2018 on Twin, and the Brain States album came out in 2025 on Disco Gecko. You may have seen him at music festivals such as Glastonbury, Boom, Ozora, Anthropos, Schiev, Samsara, Utiopia, or CTM. His influences include Leftfield, Eno, Massive Attack, and John Cage, an uplifting mixture of gentle groove and spiritual tranquillity. His research projects cover various subjects including club culture, sound archaeology, and songwriting.
